Player’s guide · English

Tower of the Sorcerer

The adventurer’s handbook

A thoughtful climb through fifty floors. Learn the rules, choose your battles, and keep a few surprises for the journey.

01 — 50Every step is a decision

Chapter 01

Before you enter the tower

A hero enters a tower to rescue a captive princess. It sounds familiar, but the story may not unfold as you expect. Discover the reason as you play.

Tower of the Sorcerer sits between a role-playing game and a puzzle. There is no random element: the same actions in the same situation produce the same result. Take your time, think ahead, and choose the order in which you spend health, gold and keys.

Chapter 02

Movement, items and saving

Movement and items

Move with the arrow keys or WASD, or click a destination on the map. Click routes follow clear roads and stop at obstacles; selecting an enemy or door directly can make it the final action. Use the inventory to activate items, and Enter or Space to advance dialogue. Settings contains language, audio, animation speed and portable-save options.

Autosaves and checkpoints

Accepted game actions autosave. After acquiring the Hero Orb, "Save game" keeps a separate checkpoint and Settings can export a portable save. "Restore checkpoint" returns to your saved checkpoint. Detailed enemy information and battle forecasts also require the Hero Orb.

Chapter 03

Understanding your status

Your status at a glance
IndicatorMeaning
FloorYour current place in the fifty-floor tower.
Health · HPDamage reduces health; reaching zero ends the game. Potions and altar offerings restore it.
Attack · ATKDetermines how much damage you deal. Red crystals, swords and altar offerings increase it.
Defense · DEFReduces damage from ordinary attacks. Blue crystals, shields and altar offerings increase it.
GoldEarned by defeating enemies. Spend it at altars or trade with merchants.
KeysOpening a colored door spends one key of the matching color: yellow, blue or red.
EquipmentThe weapon and shield displays show your current equipment. Swords raise attack; shields raise defense.
InventoryShows the special items you have collected. Select an item to use its ability.
InformationEnemy information, status messages and conversations explain what is happening around you.

Chapter 04

Think before you fight

Walking into an enemy begins a battle. In an ordinary battle, you strike first, then the enemy retaliates. Attacks alternate until one side reaches zero health. If you win, you take the enemy’s gold.

Ordinary battles, without an item multiplier. HP = health · ATK = attack · DEF = defense. Your values are green; the enemy’s values are red.

01 · Your damage per hit

Hero ATK−Enemy DEF

Your base attack must be greater than the enemy’s defense to begin the fight.

02 · Damage from one enemy retaliation

max(Enemy ATK−Hero DEF,0)

max means “take the larger value”. If your defense blocks the attack, you lose no HP.

03 · Number of enemy retaliations

⌊Enemy HP−1Your damage per hit⌋

⌊ ⌋ means round down. The enemy does not retaliate after your killing blow.

04 · Total health lost

Retaliations×Damage per retaliation

Use the results of steps 02 and 03.

05 · The survival check

Hero HP>Total health lost

Equal is not enough: reaching zero HP is fatal. Special encounters may strike first or follow scripted rules.

Worked example · a three-hit victory

Hero

ATK 15 · DEF 12 · HP to be checked

Example enemy

HP 30 · ATK 18 · DEF 5

  1. Your damage per hit15 − 5 = 10 HP
  2. Damage per retaliation18 − 12 = 6 HP
  3. Enemy retaliations⌊ (30 − 1) ÷ 10 ⌋ = 2
  4. Total health lost2 × 6 = 12 HP

You need at least 13 HP to survive. At 13 HP, you finish with 1 HP.

The Cross and similar items affect only certain creatures. Their extra strength is not a universal increase against every enemy.

Chapter 05

Spend your strength wisely

You cannot win simply by killing every creature and collecting every item. A treasure may be visible but expensive to reach. Decide what to collect now, what to leave for later, and which enemies you can avoid.

  • Avoid unnecessary fights, especially before your equipment improves.
  • Compare the health cost of a route with the strength or resources it gives you.
  • Return to earlier floors when improved attack or defense makes their enemies cheaper to defeat.
  • Listen to people in the tower. Information that seems unhelpful now may matter later.

Chapter 06

Special items

These items help you explore the tower, remember clues and overcome obstacles. Open the acquisition hints when you want to know where to find them.

Orb of the Hero

Compares your strength with an enemy’s and forecasts the battle result. It also enables manual save checkpoints and portable-save export. Remember that the Cross and similar items help only against the creatures they affect.

Acquisition hint · spoiler

Speak with the old man on floor 3.

Orb of Wisdom

Records the old-man and merchant hints that you first hear while owning the orb. The journal has 24 possible hints, and reviewing them can make a puzzling clue clearer. Earlier conversations are not added retroactively, even if you return to the speaker. Click the orb or open the journal to review recorded hints; the orb is reusable. It is a different item from the Hero Orb.

Acquisition hint · spoiler

It is on floor 6, guarded by Skeleton B.

Orb of Flight

Use it beside stairs to travel to floors you have already visited. It can be used repeatedly without being exhausted, saving you the climb back through familiar passages.

Acquisition hint · spoiler

It is on floor 1, guarded by Skeleton B.

Magic Mattock

Makes openings in the walls around you. Try different places: an unexpected opening may be more valuable than a direct route.

Acquisition hint · spoiler

It appears after defeating the Giant Octopus on floor 16.

Magic Elixir

Restores health according to your attack and defense at the moment you drink it. Its timing matters: using it after becoming stronger can yield more health.

Acquisition hint · spoiler

Someone already has this item and may be willing to give it to you.

Destruction Ball

A bomb for destroying enemies on the four neighboring sides, including opponents too costly to fight normally. It does not work against every enemy.

Warp Staff

Moves you to another place on the same floor. Like the Mattock, it can reveal surprising ways through the tower.

Destination and charges

The destination mirrors your position through the center of the 11 × 11 map: using zero-based coordinates, (x, y) becomes (10 − x, 10 − y). It must be ordinary road. A charge is spent even when the destination is blocked.

Chapter 07

Meeting the fairies

A fairy appears after you clear a major area. Speak with her to continue your journey.

Keeping a checkpoint

Once you have the Hero Orb, use "Save game" when you want to keep a checkpoint to return to. A fairy conversation does not create a separate checkpoint for you.

Chapter 08

A route through the first area

This route through floors 1–10 prioritizes equipment and defense before tackling tougher enemies.

Reveal the floor 1–10 walkthrough · spoilers

Avoid unnecessary fights. In particular, do not fight the armed Skeleton before obtaining a shield.

  1. After the introduction, head for floor 5 and collect its sword. Check the walls for a secret passage.
  2. Offer gold at the altar on floor 4 to raise defense.
  3. Gather the crystals on floors 1–5, then offer at the altar again to improve defense.
  4. Collect the shield on floor 9.
  5. Gather crystals throughout floors 1–10. Defeat enemies that cannot hurt you, collect their gold, and improve attack and defense at the altar.
  6. When ready, defeat the floor-8 gatekeepers and obtain the red key, then challenge the Skeleton boss on floor 10. You can leave one blue key and five yellow keys uncollected if necessary.

Experiment while learning. As the rules become familiar, you can work out a shorter or more efficient route yourself.

Chapter 09

The five regions of the tower

The tower has five ten-floor regions. The guide below reveals enemies and later story hints.

Reveal the region guide · later-game spoilers
The five regions
Floors / regionWhat to expect
1–10 · Skeleton corpsComparatively weak enemies teach basic tactics. The Skeleton carrying a sword and shield is a troublesome opponent.
11–20 · Immortal forceZombies and Vampires are powerful; the Cross is valuable against them. A Giant Octopus blocks the route and guards a special reward.
21–30 · Great Magic MasterThis region’s boss is very strong. Be patient; there is comparatively little else here.
31–40 · Golden Knight corpsKnights, swordsmen and soldiers make this a tough region. The Golden Knight is an unreliable speaker; a Giant Dragon presents another obstacle.
41–50 · Magic Sergeant ZenoMagical enemies dominate. Zeno orchestrated the hero’s capture in the introduction. Trying to fight this final opponent head-on will lead to destruction.
